newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu admits mistake but claims vindication.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu admits mistake but claims vindication.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu admitted on Sunday making mistakes in the appointment of an attorney general but said Israeli prosecutors had vindicated him of any criminal act.
"The bottom line is I didn't commit any crime, and the attorney general confirmed that," he said in a televised speech. "I think, and so do the majority of the people, that this affair is behind us."

Prosecutors decided on Sunday not to charge Netanyahu in a corruption scandal, saying police recommendations to indict him were based on insufficient evidence. But prosecutors did say a political ally should be indicted and others close to the Israeli leader should face further investigation.

"About the mistakes that were committed, I am sorry and I will work to correct them. I intend to learn the lessons and implement them. For me, and I think for most of the people in Israel, this affair is behind us. Now all of us must look to the future. I want to thank you for your support during this difficult period," Netanyahu said.
"I cannot deny the fact that certain damage was done to the government and I intend to act to fix this damage."
"Our government will be more open and sensitive."

"But our opponents also have to change. They have to understand that things are decided in elections, at the polling station...In a democracy, only you the voters can decide on changing the government," Netanyahu said.
Lashing out at the media and the opposition, he said: "There are people who do not like me, who do not like me in particular. And they want to erode my legitimacy as the prime minister.
"But at base the attacks against me come from one central motive: an attempt to overthrow the government because of our opponents' fundamental disagreement with our path," he said.

"They refuse to accept the fact that the people voted for us and not for them. They refuse to accept the fact that we are building on Har Homa, they refuse to accept our efforts to protect the unity of Jerusalem, they refuse to accept our vigorous opposition to a Palestinian state. They refuse to accept that we are guarding the Golan and not coming down from it," Netanyahu said.
"In short, they refuse to accept your, the voters', decision in the last elections.
"They will not succeed in this...I will continue to speak in your name and further the principles that brought you to vote for me...I have no doubt that together we can achieve those goals.

"But I cannot deny the fact that a certain amount of damage was caused to the government. And I intend to act to repair this damage. I specifically intend to do a house cleaning, an internal house cleaning, and repair all that needs to be repaired."
